White Noise · A support exchange in public

20 relays meet a 16-relay limit

A failed group invitation exposes two separate problems: a relay-directory limit that stops the operation, and an earlier bug that replaced a user’s relay list instead of adding to it.

From Sondre’s report and Max’s replies

The invitation failed before Sondre could join the btc++ group. White Noise’s error named a specific obstacle: relay endpoint count 20 exceeds limit 16. The report describes a confusing sequence of relay-list changes, a successful invitation to a small group, and a failure after the previous relays were restored.

Max’s reply puts the immediate cause in the inbox list, which had twenty relays against White Noise’s current limit of sixteen. But the reply also acknowledges that rejecting the whole operation is a bug: There is still the bug that we're failing hard. Key packages might have been available from a smaller selection of those relays.

That matters because the complaint is not simply that somebody chose too many servers. It is also about what an application does when it encounters more than it is prepared to handle. The reported error concerns relay endpoints; it is not a sixteen-person limit on the group.

A separate reply addresses the earlier replacement of the user’s relay list. Max says: There was a bug that instead of adding it replaced. But that's fixed already. The same reply recommends retaining existing relays and adding one suited to larger events and more concurrent connections.

In a broader public note, Max recommends three to five relays, arguing that long lists increase the bandwidth and connection work required of other clients. That recommendation and the acknowledged failure behaviour are different parts of the story. Reducing a list may avoid the limit; handling the limit gracefully remains work for the application.

The replies report the relay-list replacement bug fixed. They do not report a shipped fix for the invitation’s hard failure.

A postcard from Morocco

Couscous, then a free ride

There was another gift on the trip: a taxi driver gave Jurjen a ride for free. The note praises the hospitality encountered in Morocco.

Posted in this reading window; the meal is described as having happened on Friday.

From the workshop

Zapstore

An indexer change on the way to v2

Zapstore announced a pause in external updates while it replaces its indexing software. Self-publishing is unaffected.

The project says it has chosen one stable signing key per app, will honour key rotations, and is prioritising self-signed apps over external builds such as F-Droid. It describes this as the first step towards v2.

No completion notice appears in this reading.

Quill & Omostrich

The phone builds. The laptop signs.

Tim describes an Android client that builds unsigned Nostr events on the phone and sends them through Tailscale to Omostrich on a laptop. The signer returns the signed event; the phone publishes it.

A subsequent Quill update adds a My Notes tab, a three-column feed switcher, Blossom media support and cold-start performance fixes. The stated design stays the same: the private signing key remains off the phone.

Field report · Covington, Kentucky

Charge the car. Bring a broom.

Jasonb visited Distributed Charge’s demonstration EV charger in a borrowed Tesla and found a working payment experiment with cobwebs attached.

The account describes a 25,000-sat initial deposit, payments by QR code, and the deposit returned after the consumed energy was paid for. Charging was slower than at a Tesla Supercharger, but the visit made the small-payment proposition tangible: electricity bought directly with sats.

This is the visitor’s account of the demo, not a general tariff or performance test.

Keeping a record

The drawing desk

Bangkok, busy on the page

Language & preservation

A small language needs a place online

The Internet Archive highlights Peter Scholing’s account of preserving Papiamento’s written and audiovisual heritage with the National Library of Aruba.

The post names Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, and the pressure smaller languages face as English and Spanish dominate online. Scholing’s contribution, The Wind-Blown Language: Papiamento, appears in the Archive’s Vanishing Culture report. The source note points to the chapter and a print edition.

Sound

The scissors move into the browser

After learning to splice physical tape last week, bitpunk.fm made a digital cut-up tool. The author says the work happens entirely in the browser, without uploading audio to a server.

It is a small translation from one way of making sound to another: the old technique supplies the idea, and a browser makes it easier to try.

In brief · On the calendar · The exchange

Walks need new pins

BitcoinWalk asks Hannover organisers to resubmit their walk as it moves to a Nostr-native app and prepares to retire the old website. A separate request goes to Graz. The migration is also a reminder that moving a platform still requires moving its local knowledge.

Five harvests in one order

GrowMilkweedPlants added 2024 common milkweed seed to an order from an education-domain email address, completing a run from 2021 through 2025. The seller suspects an experiment comparing seed ages; that purpose is not confirmed.

88 requests paid for

Noderunners Radio reports 365 songs in its daily tally, with eighty-eight requested and paid for by listeners. Three payments went straight to the artist.

The pantry

Mustard, fruit, honey

Jimble’s Jumble lists chunky piccalilli and a hotter chilli version at £5 per 280 g jar. Both are active UK listings.

The same maker’s blackberry, cherry and vanilla preserve is also £5, with at least 340 g per jar. Reused glass may vary in shape; the listing specifies new lids.

Staci offers Cretan wildflower honey in 4 oz jars for 5,000 sats, with a wooden dipper, or 10 oz jars for 15,000 sats.

Prices are as listed. Check delivery options with each seller.

The Instrument

400 notes, zero in common

The ranked notes desk and the anonymous control each returned four hundred notes from the same window. Their overlap was zero. Across fourteen desks queried, today’s reading contains 631 events from 227 voices.

Twenty-four hours ending Wednesday, October 7 at 13:05, Europe/Vilnius. These counts describe the reading, not the whole network.

And finally

The paper prototype survives

Megistus describes making games with their son: a card game invented on paper over the summer has become a digital one. The first working version needed neither a relay directory nor a release pipeline.
